[ASSISTANT_SAID] The first commercial country music recordings were made in the 1920s, with artists such as Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family leading the way.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family's songs told stories of love, heartbreak, and rural life.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Country music grew in popularity in the 1930s with the rise of radio and the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville as a hub for the genre.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1940s, country music shifted towards a more polished sound known as the "Nashville Sound," with artists like Patsy Cline and Hank Williams.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1960s saw the emergence of the Bakersfield Sound, featuring artists like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard, focusing on a raw, traditional approach.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1970s and 1980s, artists like Dolly Parton and Willie Nelson combined various music styles, including rock and pop, with traditional country music.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Today, artists like Luke Bryan and Miranda Lambert incorporate more rock and pop elements into their music while honoring country music's roots.
